programme.desc: Vacationers think they've found the perfect place for a bachelor party, but a deadly, flesh-eating virus is waiting to infect them.

programme.title: Feral
programme.desc: A wild animal attacks six grad students on a weekend hike in the woods. One by one, they become infected with an unknown virus that turns them into bloodthirsty creatures.

programme.title: Yummy
programme.desc: A young couple travel to a shabby Eastern European hospital for plastic surgery. Once there, things unravel into blood and violence.

programme.title: Airborne
programme.desc: A plane takes off during a snowstorm and soon reports both pilots are dead. As the passengers slowly die off, they wish they had never left the ground.

programme.title: State of Emergency
programme.desc: Survivors band together after an explosion at a military bioweapons plant turns most of their neighbors into flesh-eating zombies.

programme.title: Dementia
programme.desc: Hired as a live-in nurse, a seemingly sweet woman (Kristina Klebe) unleashes her dark side as she torments a Vietnam War veteran (Gene Jones) who has dementia.

programme.title: Extraterrestrial
programme.desc: Malevolent aliens interrupt five collegians' vacation at a remote woodland cabin.

programme.title: #Horror
programme.desc: Preteen girls face a night of terror when their obsession with a disturbing online game goes too far.

programme.title: The Shed
programme.desc: A teen and his best friend endure nonstop torment from bullies at school, but that soon changes when one discovers a bloodthirsty creature that resides in a country shed.

programme.title: ATM
programme.desc: A murderous assailant traps three people (Alice Eve, Josh Peck, Brian Geraghty) in a small kiosk containing an automatic teller machine.

programme.title: Centigrade
programme.desc: A man and his pregnant wife become trapped in their car when a storm buries them underneath layers of snow and ice. As supplies dwindle and temperatures plunge, the couple must battle the elements and hypothermia in a desperate fight for survival.

programme.title: The Clovehitch Killer
programme.desc: After Tyler finds a cache of disturbing images in his father's possession, he begins to suspect that the man he trusts most in the world may be responsible for a series of unsolved murders.

programme.title: Feral
programme.desc: A wild animal attacks six grad students on a weekend hike in the woods. One by one, they become infected with an unknown virus that turns them into bloodthirsty creatures.

programme.title: Nobody Gets Out Alive

programme.title: I Trapped the Devil
programme.desc: Hoping for a joyful family reunion, Matt and his wife pay a surprise visit to the home of his estranged brother, Steve, to celebrate Christmas. To their shock, they soon learn that Steve has a hostage in his basement -- a man he claims is the devil.

programme.title: May The Devil Take You Too
programme.desc: Two years after escaping from a demonic terror, Alfie and Nara try to continue their lives, but Alfie is still haunted by feelings of guilt and unnatural visions.

programme.title: Baghead
programme.desc: A young woman inherits a run-down pub and discovers a dark secret within its basement, Baghead, a shape-shifting creature that lets one speak to lost loved ones, but not without consequence.

programme.title: A Wounded Fawn
programme.desc: A serial killer brings an unsuspecting new victim on a weekend getaway to add another body to his ever-growing count. She's buying into his faux charms, and he's eagerly lusting for blood.

programme.title: Hellbender
programme.desc: A teen and her mother live simply in a home in the woods, spending their time making metal music. A chance encounter with a fellow teen causes her to uncover a connection between her family and witchcraft, which causes a rift with her mother.

programme.title: May The Devil Take You Too
programme.desc: Two years after escaping from a demonic terror, Alfie and Nara try to continue their lives, but Alfie is still haunted by feelings of guilt and unnatural visions.

programme.title: The Vigil
programme.desc: Terror strikes when an Orthodox Jewish man agrees to watch over the dead body of a community member in a dilapidated Brooklyn home.

programme.title: I Remember You

programme.title: Simon King's Shetland Adventure
programme.desc: Simon King, wildlife cameraman and Springwatch presenter, is fulfilling a boyhood dream and experiencing the Shetland Islands with his family through the changing seasons. Simon is enjoying the islands at their best, with 19 hours of glorious sunlight, the remarkable 'simmer dim' - the Shetland term for the midnight gloaming - and a plethora of wildlife. His expensive high-speed camera breaks, but with a little help from the locals, he manages to get it repaired and uses it to capture some wonderful footage of powerful gannets diving for fish. He also follows an otter family's poignant separation as the one-year-old cub is pushed away by his mother to lead an independent life. Shetland has more than lived up to Simon's expectations for wilderness and given his family an experience they will never forget. The visit ends with a sighting of a pod of killer whales, just metres away from where he is standing. A suitable end to a great trip.

programme.title: Natural World
programme.desc: The endearing pangolin is a little-known scaly mammal. Found in Africa and Asia, these shy creatures have an unfortunate tagline - they are the most poached and illegally trafficked animals in the world. Based in Namibia, conservationist Maria Diekmann rescues and rehabilitates her local pangolins. In a bid to better understand the global issues they are facing, we follow Maria to Vietnam, Thailand and China into the very heart of the crisis, where demand for pangolin products is greatest. In what turns out to be an emotional journey, Maria joins forces with a Chinese megastar to build a campaign to bring awareness to the plight of an animal most people have never even heard of.

programme.title: The Arctic Convoy
programme.desc: 1942. A civilian cargo ship’s hardline captain clashes with his more humane first mate on a mission to Murmansk, which is made more dangerous when their convoy must scatter. Tense war drama inspired by a true story. In Norwegian with English subtitles.

programme.title: To the Manor Born

programme.title: Keeping Up Appearances

programme.title: Timeshift
programme.desc: Timeshift digs into the archive to discover the unwritten rules that have governed the way we drink in Britain. In the pubs and working men's clubs of the 40s and 50s there were strict customs governing who stood where. To be invited to sup at the bar was a rite of passage for many young men, and it took years for women to be accepted into these bastions of masculinity. As the country prospered and foreign travel became widely available, so new drinking habits were introduced as we discovered wine and, even more exotically, cocktails. People began to drink at home as well as at work, where journalists typified a tradition of the liquid lunch. Advertising played its part as lager was first sold as a woman's drink and then the drink of choice for young men with a bit of disposable income. The rules changed and changed again, but they were always there - unwritten and unspoken, yet underwriting our complicated relationship with drinking.

programme.title: BBC Young Musician
programme.desc: The live auditions continue, and the judges face tough decisions about who to put through to the competition’s quarter-final. Making that choice are world-famous concert pianist, educator and curator Joanna MacGregor, conductor and broadcaster Ben Gernon, and guest judge trombonist Peter Moore. Peter knows only too well what it feels like to compete in BBC Young Musician, as at just 12, he became the youngest ever winner. Broadcaster and writer Petroc Trelawny presents from the live auditions filmed earlier this year at Bath Spa University. Featuring the best young classical musicians from across the UK playing a range of instruments, from marimba to bassoon, piano to French horn, cello to clarinet. We hear music from Mozart, Liszt and Elgar, together with musical treats from lesser-known composers. At the end of the programme, the judges reveal the names of the eight musicians they want to see and hear again in the next round. Five places will be the representatives from each instrumental family - keyboard, strings, wind, brass and percussion - and three wildcard places are also up for grabs. With so much talent on display, who has done enough to get through to the quarter-final?

programme.title: Talking Shakespeare
programme.desc: Celia Imrie takes a trip through the BBC’s archive for a celebration of the works of Shakespeare, and an exploration into how the Bard’s biggest plays have been brought to cinema and television screens over the years. It’s a story that’s told through a selection of interviews with stars from the 1950s right up to the present day, with anecdotes and insights revealing how Shakespeare’s plays have been continuously adapted to suit each new generation, capturing changing attitudes to race and gender. Amongst those featured are the established acting knights Olivier and Gielgud, dames Helen Mirren, Judi Dench and Maggie Smith, and the latest wave of big names, including David Tennant, David Harewood and Maxine Peake.

programme.title: Remembers...
programme.desc: With an acting career that started in the 1970s, Lesley Manville is an established star of stage and screen, with TV roles ranging from Emmerdale to Harlots, films such as High Hopes and Phantom Thread, and a stage career ranging from the RSC to the forefront of British writing at the famous Royal Court theatre. She is perfectly placed to tell us about Caryl Churchill’s Top Girls, a play that quickly established itself as a landmark in British theatre. In 1982, she was part of the original cast, a production that garnered awards and a Broadway transfer. In 1991, she played the lead in a BBC version helmed by the show’s original director, Max Stafford Clark. Lesley tells us about her memories of the original stage show - how a cast that included Gwen Taylor and Lyndsay Duncan came to be aware of the power of what they were involved in. She explains some of the themes behind Churchill’s writing, the rise of Thatcherism and the impact it had on feminism. She discusses the cast, her memories of filming and the difference between acting the piece on stage as opposed to TV. But mostly, she reinforces the legacy of Churchill’s work, not just in this country but around the world.

programme.title: Performance
programme.desc: Seven actresses take sixteen roles in this uncompromising assessment of high-profile and low-profile women, part fantasy, part hard-nosed reality. Marlene celebrates her new position as managing director of the Top Girls Appointment Agency by giving a dinner party for five oddly assorted women from centuries past. But Marlene's own past will throw a question mark over her Top Girls success. Author Caryl Churchill describes her play as 'a celebration of the extraordinary achievements of women'.

programme.title: Omnibus
programme.desc: Portrait of Caryl Churchill, one of Britain's most prolific and versatile playwrights. Featuring extracts from her plays.

programme.title: Shakespeare in Italy
programme.desc: Francesco da Mosto takes to the Italian road again in search of Shakespeare in Italy. From Romeo and Juliet to the jealousy of Othello, Shakespeare used the land of love to tell his most passionate stories about falling in love. Needless to say, along the way Francesco adds some insights of his own and revels in claims that not only did Shakespeare visit Italy, but also was born in Sicily. It's a whole new take on the Bard!

programme.title: New Zealand: Earth's Mythical Islands
programme.desc: Isolated since the time of the dinosaurs, New Zealand's wildlife has been left to its own devices, with surprising consequences. Its ancient forests are still stalked by predators from the Jurassic era. It's also one of the most geologically active countries on earth. From Kiwis with their giant eggs, to forest-dwelling penguins and helicopter-riding sheep dogs, meet the astonishing creatures and resilient people who must rise to the challenges of their beautiful, dramatic and demanding home.

programme.title: Art of France
programme.desc: Andrew Graham-Dixon explores how art in France took a dramatic turn following the French Revolution that ushered in a bold new world. From the execution of King Louis XVI and the rise of Napoleon Bonaparte - a figure who simultaneously repelled and inspired artists of his time - through to the rise of Romanticism and an art of seduction, sex and high drama, Andrew explores artists including Jacques-Louis David - whose art appeared on the barricades and in the streets - as well as the work of Delacroix, Ingres and the tragic but brilliant Theodore Gericault.

programme.title: Classic Mastermind
programme.desc: Magnus Magnusson presents the quiz programme from Keele University. The specialist subjects are Otto von Bismarck, Ernest Hemingway, myths and legends of King Arthur, and the Church of England.

programme.title: Call My Bluff

programme.title: The Sky at Night
programme.desc: Maggie Aderin explores how dyslexia has affected her life and career by meeting other dyslexic astronomers and discovering their research – from icy moons to clumpy galaxies.

programme.title: Reflecting Skin
programme.desc: Documentary presented by Bonnie Greer on how black people have been represented in western art, from medieval black Madonnas, through the great masters to modern fashion.

programme.title: Leonardo da Vinci
programme.desc: Leonardo works as a military engineer, designs fanciful flying machines, studies light and shadow, investigates gravity, dissects cadavers and pens treatises on a vast array of subjects, all while seeking the perfect patron. In Florence, Milan, Rome and finally France, he pours the sum of his scientific and artistic knowledge into a portrait that will become the most famous painting on earth. A film by Ken Burns, Sarah Burns and David McMahon.

programme.title: Clive Myrie's African Adventure
programme.desc: The second leg of Clive’s adventure takes him to Durban, known for its fabulous surfing beaches and chilled atmosphere. It’s also the biggest city in the spectacular KwaZulu-Natal province, ancestral home of the Zulu people. Clive jumps into action as he joins an anti-poaching team saving South Africa’s critically endangered rhinos from extinction and joins a surf school that teaches homeless and disadvantaged kids the skills to surf – and to transform their lives. Back in the city, Clive gets a lesson in making spicy bunny chow, the iconic street food created by Durban’s large Indian population, before heading out to the Valley of a Thousand Hills for a masterclass in Zulu beadwork at a craft centre that gives women living with HIV the skills to support their families.

programme.title: The Media Show
programme.desc: Six months after Péter Magyar's election ended Viktor Orbán's 16-year rule, Hungary's new government faces scrutiny over its promised press reforms. BBC East and Central Europe Correspondent Nick Thorpe reports from Budapest on how the country's media is changing. Broadcaster Anneka Rice reflects on fifty years since joining the BBC as a trainee, tracing her career across television and radio and the changes she has witnessed in British broadcasting. As the Cornell rape investigation continues, journalism experts including Dr Robert Topinka of Birkbeck, University of London, and Professor Kathleen Bartzen Culver of the University of Wisconsin-Madison consider the ethical and legal responsibilities of reporters covering sensitive cases.

programme.title: Talking Business
programme.desc: Record-high diesel prices caused by the wars in Iran and Ukraine have triggered rising unrest across Europe. As fears grow over the impact this energy crisis will have on inflation, what will it all mean for Europe's economy? Ben Thompson hears from European Commission Energy spokesperson Anna-Kaisa Itkonen about the significance of the G7 group of advanced economies releasing some of their reserves; Dr Michal Meidan, who is head of China energy research at the Oxford Institute for Energy Studies on the impact of Beijing’s export controls; and former deputy director of the International Monetary Fund Mohamed El-Erian on what it might mean for the global economy and how businesses and consumers can make ends meet. Plus, the CEO of Burmester Audiosysteme, Thorsten Poenig, explains the challenges of selling German technology in China.

Ben Thompson hears from European Commission Energy spokesperson Anna-Kaisa Itkonen about the significance of the G7 group of advanced economies releasing some of their reserves; Dr Michal Meidan, who is head of China energy research at the Oxford Institute for Energy Studies on the impact of Beijing’s export controls; and former deputy director of the International Monetary Fund Mohamed El-Erian on what it might mean for the global economy and how businesses and consumers can make ends meet. Plus, the CEO of Burmester Audiosysteme, Thorsten Poenig, explains the challenges of selling German technology in China.

programme.title: The Media Show
programme.desc: Six months after Péter Magyar's election ended Viktor Orbán's 16-year rule, Hungary's new government faces scrutiny over its promised press reforms. BBC East and Central Europe Correspondent Nick Thorpe reports from Budapest on how the country's media is changing. Broadcaster Anneka Rice reflects on fifty years since joining the BBC as a trainee, tracing her career across television and radio and the changes she has witnessed in British broadcasting. As the Cornell rape investigation continues, journalism experts including Dr Robert Topinka of Birkbeck, University of London, and Professor Kathleen Bartzen Culver of the University of Wisconsin-Madison consider the ethical and legal responsibilities of reporters covering sensitive cases.

What began as a demand for accountability has grown into a nationwide student-led protest movement against corruption, exposing deep divisions over governance, transparency and Serbia's future direction. programme.title: Clive Myrie's African Adventure
programme.desc: The second leg of Clive’s adventure takes him to Durban, known for its fabulous surfing beaches and chilled atmosphere. It’s also the biggest city in the spectacular KwaZulu-Natal province, ancestral home of the Zulu people. Clive jumps into action as he joins an anti-poaching team saving South Africa’s critically endangered rhinos from extinction and joins a surf school that teaches homeless and disadvantaged kids the skills to surf – and to transform their lives. Back in the city, Clive gets a lesson in making spicy bunny chow, the iconic street food created by Durban’s large Indian population, before heading out to the Valley of a Thousand Hills for a masterclass in Zulu beadwork at a craft centre that gives women living with HIV the skills to support their families.

programme.title: Mary at 90: A Lifetime of Cooking
programme.desc: If Mary has one passion that comes close to cooking, it’s her lifelong love of gardening. So it’s not surprising that Mary has formed a friendship with one of the country’s most respected gardening experts, Alan Titchmarsh. To celebrate her 90th year, Alan has invited Mary for a very special look behind the walls of his magnificent four-acre garden. In these magical surroundings, Mary shows Alan snippets of her old TV shows - how she used to picnic 50 years ago and how she made use of the basic veg of the 1970s. Mary and Alan then make some of her most mouthwatering recipes inspired by what we grow: an updated version of a delicious creamy cauliflower soup, Mary’s classic smoked salmon, asparagus and dill spaghetti, a salad based around the popular burrata cheese, and teriyaki tuna with ribbon salad. Finally, it's Alan’s chance to make a cake for the first time - Mary’s classic apple cake served with cream.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Christina Trevanion presents from Shrewsbury, where experts Philip Serrell and Izzie Balmer join the teams as they search for the best items to sell at auction in Lichfield. Christina visits Shrewsbury Abbey to discover more about the restoration of the abbey’s century-old organ.

programme.title: The Football Interview
programme.desc: The Football Interview sees the biggest names in sport and entertainment join host Kelly Somers for bold, in-depth conversations about the nation’s favourite sport. We explore mindset and motivation, reflect on defining moments and career highs, and discuss personal insights. It’s a chance to show an honest, human and sometimes surprising side to familiar faces. At the heart of this is Kelly Somers – one of the most trusted, versatile and authentic voices in sports broadcasting. Kelly brings a brand of warmth and relatability that resonates with both athletes and audiences. What sets her apart is her ability to dig deeper with a sensitive approach, creating a space where athletes feel comfortable being open, honest and at times vulnerable. Each episode sees Kelly draw out stories and insight from the player behind the name about the beautiful game, their origins and values, and a look-ahead to the future from a sporting and personal perspective. She takes her subjects on a journey – and takes the viewer with her.

Newlyweds Shrek and Fiona face their first marital hurdle when the sudden death of King Harold means Shrek himself is next in line. However, with fatherhood looming, Shrek is reluctant. He decides to try and find the true heir - Fiona's errant, rebellious cousin. But while Shrek and his faithful companions Donkey and Puss in Boots go off in search of the heir, handsome rogue Prince Charming stages a coup at the castle. Featuring the voices of Mike Myers (Shrek), Eddie Murphy (Donkey), Cameron Diaz (Princess Fiona), Antonio Banderas (Puss in Boots), Julie Andrews (Queen Lillian), John Cleese (King Harold), Rupert Everett (Prince Charming), Eric Idle (Merlin), Justin Timberlake (Artie), John Krasinski (Lancelot), Ian McShane (Captain Hook) and Amy Poehler (Snow White).

Chris Yeo flexes his muscles with a piece of vintage mail order gym kit, and Hilary Kay is thrilled to find an early 20th-century Jemima Puddle-duck doll inspired by Beatrix Potter. Fiona Bruce explores the history of the estate, home to Leonard and Dorothy Elmhirst and the 'Dartington experiment', which made it a haven for artists, writers and thinkers in the early 20th century. programme.desc: Flo and Sue are in Stevenage to help mother and daughter Margaret and Elizabeth transform their south-facing garden. While blessed with sunlight, the space is currently a chaotic jumble of mismatched plant pots, overgrown bushes and uneven, sloped steps, making it overwhelming and difficult to enjoy. Their dream is to turn it into a mother–daughter retreat with a serene, shaded relaxation garden. Elizabeth and Margaret envision a charming pergola draped in delicate vines, offering a peaceful spot to unwind together. Wider, gently sloping steps and accessible raised beds will allow Margaret to continue her beloved gardening safely, while lush, in-ground plants reduce maintenance. They also hope for privacy screening and planting that discreetly hides the shed at the back of the garden. Elizabeth juggles a demanding full-time job with caring for her ageing mother, leaving little time to work on the garden. Margaret is retired and longing to enjoy the outdoors, but her partial sight makes the current low-lying plants and treacherous steps a real obstacle to relaxation and upkeep. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

She then discovers that this particular social craze may not be so modern after all as she follows a trail that leads her to Wolverhampton Wanderers and a bizarre revelation that the FA Cup final in 1939 was nicknamed the 'Monkey Gland Final' after several players had testosterone-boosting injections before the game. Richard Hammond is on the shores of Lake Como testing the exciting new Alfa Romeo 4C, a mid-engined machine from one of the world's most beloved sports car makers. Hammond's enjoyment of the super-lightweight, 237-horsepower beauty is brought to an abrupt halt by the arrival of Jeremy Clarkson on a quad bike, demanding a race to the far end of the vast lake. Elsewhere in the programme, Clarkson is in the genteel surroundings of Bruges, and at the rather less sedate Spa Grand Prix track in order to test a thrilling new breed of hybrid hypercar: the stunning 904-horsepower McLaren P1. Meanwhile, James May is at the vast Camp Bastion in Afghanistan looking at the incredible efforts behind the army's largest vehicle redeployment since the Second World War. Finally, actor Tom Hiddleston, star of Thor, The Avengers and War Horse, tries his hand out on the track as the Star in the Reasonably Priced Car.

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc: Why are more younger people getting cancer? Rates of bowel, breast and other cancers are rising among younger generations according to NHS data. Hayley Hassall meets patients facing devastating diagnoses and investigates what may be driving the increase. From ultra-processed food and changing diets to chemicals found in everyday products, Panorama examines the latest scientific research into possible causes and asks whether regulators and government are doing enough to protect public health.

programme.title: Secrets of the Bayeux Tapestry: Inside the Museum
programme.desc: The Bayeux Tapestry is one of the treasures of the medieval world. Across 70 metres of exquisitely embroidered scenes, it tells the story of one of the most seismic events in British history – the Norman Invasion of 1066. For the last 950 years, this crucial part of Britain's national story has remained on the other side of the English Channel, in Bayeux, Normandy, but now it’s coming back to the UK. A stellar cast of historians and experts follow the painstaking efforts to bring this priceless work of art back to the UK, where experts believe it was made, for a once-in-a-millennium exhibition at the British Museum.

As he prunes roses, stores the apple harvest and plants out spring cabbages in the kitchen garden, he also turns his attention to next year, sharing ideas for bulbs that will bring colour and life to a shady border. Rachel de Thame visits a specialist wildflower nursery to discover how these beautiful plants can transform our gardens while providing a vital lifeline for wildlife. programme.desc: Wildlife expert Saba Douglas-Hamilton, together with her husband Frank and their three young children, moves to the romantic Samburu National Reserve in Kenya to run a safari camp for the first time. But life out there isn't easy. There are monkeys in the kitchen, floods threatening the camp and, with no fences to keep out the wildlife, elephants are regular house guests. This series follows their ups and downs as the family struggles to keep guests, elephants, lions and even crocodiles smiling. The team gear up to celebrate the end of the tourist season Samburu-style. With the rains on their way, Saba and the team watch over elephant mothers about to give birth as Frank and David try to safeguard the future of Samburu's spectacular wildlife.

programme.title: A Matter of Life and Death
programme.desc: Returning to England from a bombing run in May 1945, flyer Peter Carter's plane is damaged and his parachute ripped to shreds. He has his crew bail out safely but figures it is curtains for himself. He gets on the radio and talks to June, a young American woman working for the USAAF, and they are quite moved by each other's voices. Peter then jumps, preferring this to burning up with his plane. He wakes up in the surf. It was his time to die, but there was a mix-up in heaven - they couldn't find him in all that fog. By the time his 'conductor' catches up with him, Peter and June have met and fallen in love. This changes everything, and since it happened through no fault of his own, Peter figures that heaven owes him a second chance. Heaven agrees to a trial to decide his fate.

programme.title: Marcus Wareing's Tales from a Kitchen Garden
programme.desc: Setting out to bring in new livestock and expand his range of produce, Marcus turns his attention to the smallholding's disused chicken coop. In search of the tastiest chicken, as well as some tips on how to rear them, he heads to Leicestershire to meet farmers Nick and Jacob. Back on the smallholding, he gets a lesson in cultivating his own mushroom patch, before welcoming some chickens of his own. He also checks out the local vineyard, getting a lesson on English wines and a free tasting of what the neighbours are producing. This delicious find is the perfect accompaniment for a feast that celebrates the new arrivals.

programme.title: Nadiya’s Everyday Baking
programme.desc: Roasts easy enough for any day of the week. A set of lamb ribs in a pineapple and coriander marinade make for the perfect family feast, and roast chicken gets a punchy kimchi and miso makeover.

programme.title: Natural World
programme.desc: A tale of life on the Zambezi River, set against the epic backdrop of Victoria Falls. The story is told from the point of view of a local fisherman, Mr White, who has fished these waters for 69 years, and whose riverside companions are elephants, baboons, hippos and kingfishers. Follow the fortunes of these animals through his eyes, and learn how their lives are ruled by the moods of the river and the rains.

programme.title: Emma
programme.desc: Emma Woodhouse, wealthy and beautiful, searches for a new companion when her beloved governess, Miss Taylor, gets married. She settles on Harriet Smith and becomes determined to make a match for her. However, Emma's father and her dear friend Mr Knightley caution her against her plans.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: This episode comes from the culturally rich north east as Anita Manning and Nick Davies descend upon the Discovery Museum, situated in the centre of Newcastle upon Tyne. Members of the public bring their antiques and collectables along to Europe's largest naval aviation museum and the antique experts share their knowledge of what everything is worth. There are some great items salvaged by a demolition worker and house clearance worker. Plus Paul finds out what the people of Tyneside make of Anthony Gormley's Angel of the North 15 years on.

programme.title: Mosquito Squadron
programme.desc: World War II drama in which an RAF pilot heads a special mission behind enemy lines to destroy a secret German weapon. However, on arriving in France, he discovers that Allied prisoners of war are being used as a human shield.

programme.title: The Great Escape
programme.desc: During the Second World War, a group of Allied prisoners of war mount a daring breakout from a supposedly inescapable Nazi prison camp. Based on a true story.

programme.title: Forty Hits of 1976 at the BBC
programme.desc: A strong contender for the title of 'weirdest year in pop', 1976 marked the birth of The Sex Pistols and saw hits from the likes of Thin Lizzy, Joan Armatrading, Dolly Parton and Wings, and had John Miles celebrating music of both the future and the past. And yet, the year's biggest-selling single was Brotherhood of Man's Eurovision-winning Kisses for Me, and the cider-loving Wurzels somehow managed to plough their way to the top of the charts. This collection captures all those musical highs and lows, alongside performances from Elton John and Kiki Dee, Cliff Richard and The Rolling Stones, as well as a special double dose of the 1970s' very own 'fab four' - ABBA.

programme.title: ABBA at the BBC
programme.desc: If you fancy an hour's worth of irresistible guilty pleasures from Anni-Frid, Benny, Bjorn and Agnetha, this is the programme for you. ABBA stormed the 1974 Eurovision Song Contest with their winning entry Waterloo, and this programme charts the meteoric rise of the band with some of their greatest performances at the BBC. It begins in 1974 with their first Top of the Pops appearance, and we even get to see the band entertaining holidaymakers in Torbay in a 1975 Seaside Special. There are many classic ABBA tunes from the 1979 BBC special ABBA in Switzerland, plus their final BBC appearance on the Late Late Breakfast show in 1982. This compilation is a must for all fans and includes great archive interviews, promos and performances of some of ABBA's classics, including Waterloo, Dancing Queen, Does Your Mother Know, Thank You for the Music, SOS, Fernando, Chiquitita and many more.

programme.title: More ABBA at the BBC
programme.desc: Another voyage into the archives for more of the Swedish supergroup’s best BBC moments. As well as looking back, this collection brings things right up to date, capturing the excitement and sounds of their recent, technologically pioneering stage shows. Sitting alongside the new material are plenty of classics that highlight Benny and Bjorn’s fondness for a song title that repeats itself: Ring, Ring, Honey, Honey, Money, Money, Money and I Do, I Do, I Do, I Do, I Do. And there's also an exclusive performance of the song So Long, which had been lost from the BBC archives and was assumed to be missing forever but has been recovered and restored, and is shown again here for the first time since its original transmission in 1974.

programme.title: Top of the Pops
programme.desc: The nation grew up with Top of the Pops, and it was always a talking point, but 35 years ago, a particular kind of Top of the Pops programme and tone held sway. This documentary explores Top of the Pops in 1976 - as a barometer of the state of pop and light entertainment TV. It celebrates the power of the programme and observes the British society of the mid-70s, British TV and the British pop scene. In 1976, glam was over and nothing had replaced it - the charts belonged to Showaddywaddy, Brotherhood of Man and The Wurzels, all to be found on Top of the Pops hosted by the Radio 1 DJs. If you wanted rock, you looked to the Old Grey Whistle Test, while outside the charts, a new scene was rumbling. Contributors include Tony Blackburn, David 'Diddy' Hamilton, Paul Morley, Toyah Willcox, Showaddywaddy, Brotherhood of Man, The Wurzels and Dave Haslam.

programme.title: Brief History of a Family
programme.desc: Psychological drama. Enigmatic 15-year-old Yan Shuo is injured in an accident caused by Tu Wei, a classmate from an affluent family. Wei invites Shuo to his house, where he impresses the Tu family and begins to feel at home. In Mandarin with English subtitles.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Matt Baker and Emily McGowan are in the Cotswolds for the biggest date in the sheepdog trialling calendar - the Supreme. The finest dogs and handlers from across the UK and Ireland go head-to-head in a thrilling showcase of instinct, skill and control. After months of training and a year of tough qualifying trials, it all comes down to this - but only one will claim the coveted title of Supreme Champion.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Landward
programme.desc: Dougie is in Easter Ross on the shores of the Cromarty Firth, where he meets the couple sowing their seed-growing business in the area’s fertile farmland. Cammy is in Angus to hear how award-winning beef farmers made the switch back to native cattle for better results. Meanwhile, Rachel continues her journey round the Buchan Coast for a lesson making fishing nets, Arlene heads to the Isle of Jura to find out how three women are making a living and living their dream, and Dougie uncloaks the hidden story of a familiar local landmark.

programme.title: Weatherman Walking
programme.desc: Derek is on a mission to find his best west Walian walks - he has 17 years' worth to choose from! For his first flashback, Derek is in Cardigan Bay, where he discovers the legend of Cantre’r Gwaelod at Sarn Cynfelyna. Derek also has a go at stand-up paddle-boarding, before finishing at the university town of Aberystwyth. On his second walk, Derek travels to Ceredigion, walking from Bwlch yr Arian, where he feeds red kites, to Devil’s Bridge, famed for its three stacked bridges. On the way, he discovers the silver and lead mining history of the area. Finally, Derek follows the course of the River Teifi between Cenarth and Cilgerran, where he learns to steer a coracle, the area’s ancient form of fishing boat, and takes part in the annual coracle races.

programme.title: Saturday Kitchen Best Bites
programme.desc: Matt Tebbutt serves up a feast of global flavours from favourite Saturday Kitchen chefs. Mike Reid serves up a classic Parisian bistro dish of steak frites with a traditional Parisian sauce, while Donal Skehan and Donna Hay whip up a light and fluffy gnocchi (or gnudi) with a fresh cherry tomato and ricotta sauce. Jack Croft and Will Murray break down how to master the art of the perfect chicken wings, Shivi Ramoutar prepares curry crab and dumplings, and Paul A Young demonstrates how to make chocolate from scratch. Finally, Hollywood superstar Stanley Tucci tucks into a choice of two food heavens at the end of the show - a traditional venison bolognese or a vibrant crown prince risotto. Meanwhile, Rick Stein heads to an infamous pudding club for an astonishing seven puddings, and the Hairy Bikers head to the picturesque salt flats of France.

programme.title: Eva Longoria: Searching for France
programme.desc: Starting in the port city of Marseilles, Eva shares a spicy half-and-half pizza with local chef and rising star Valentin Ruffali, before heading to La Ola to try a delicious blend of French and north African cuisine courtesy of chef Khouloude Ben Thayer. After enjoying the ancient and feted bouillabaisse fish broth, Eva heads out into the sun-kissed landscape to try the traditional summer vegetable dish of ratatouille and a sun-drenched salad niçoise on the Riviera at the famous Hotel du Cap.

programme.title: Nigel and Adam's Farm Kitchen
programme.desc: In this final episode, Nigel and Adam look at Britain's heritage foods - the old favourites still on our shopping lists today - and how the way they are cooked and who eats them has changed over the years. With pigs having historically provided food for British families all year round, and with every county in the country still rearing pigs, pork in its many forms, from ham to bacon and sausages, is the most popular choice of meat. So how do farmers meet our demands for pork? The boys find out by rearing their own three different breeds of pig. As the series draws to a close, Adam takes to the markets to sell off the produce to raise funds for Children in Need.

programme.title: The Ipcress File
programme.desc: Spy thriller in which intelligence agent Harry Palmer is plunged into the shabby and treacherous world of counter-espionage as he uncovers a bizarre brain drain among scientists. Based on the novel by Len Deighton.

programme.title: Funeral in Berlin
programme.desc: Harry Palmer is sent to Berlin with instructions to assist Colonel Stok, the Russian head of security for the Berlin Wall, who is eager to defect to the West. However, Palmer discovers he cannot trust anyone in the city where the double-cross is a unit of currency.

programme.title: This Farming Life
programme.desc: A new year begins, bringing new life and new experiences. Carianne and her brother-in-law Alexander take Faillish the bull to the Oban Highland Show, hoping to bag a rosette and sell him for a good price. But Carianne is nervous about being in charge. In South Ayrshire, lambing starts early with a flock of pedigree Suffolks. It’s all hands to the pump for the whole family, with the twins Cameron and Finlay rising early to help out before school. For Rachel and Camy in Inverkip, the time has come to scan their ewes to see how many are pregnant – a big moment of truth for their fledgling breeding programme. But first they must navigate the hills surrounding Dunrod Farm to find them all.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Flog It! makes Leicester's De Montfort Hall its home, and the experts hunting out the best antiques and collectables to take to auction are Claire Rawle and Thomas Plant. Paul Martin discovers a collection of Picasso ceramics put together by a legend in his own right - Lord Richard Attenborough.

programme.title: Celebrity Antiques Road Trip
programme.desc: National treasure Moira Stuart and star of stage and screen Aled Jones go head-to-head in a battle of antiques in Kent. Swapping the studio for the road, they cruise around in an all-electric Porsche 911. Helping hands on this trip are antique gurus David Harper and Serhat Ahmet. Moira shocks and surprises David with her eclectic, unorthodox choices and haggling tactics, while Aled and Serhat find common ground over sport and music. They squeeze in a stop at the town of Sandwich to hear the story of a medieval battle that would certainly have made the news, then it’s off to auction for a saleroom showdown. Who will make headline winners and who will be singing for their supper?

programme.title: Eva Longoria: Searching for France
programme.desc: Bordeaux’s world-famous vineyards are undergoing a revival as vintners seek to update their wines by introducing new technology and reinventing older traditions. Eva visits Saint-Emilion, where wine production began 1,000 years ago, and enjoys unusual wine pairings - a deep red with fish and a buttery white with cheese. But Bordeaux isn’t just about wine; it has superb produce, including succulent duck and tender beef as well as 200-million-year-old caviar, served with signature bordelaise sauces.

programme.title: Pilgrimage
programme.desc: The pilgrims' final destination is Bardsey Island, the fabled ‘Island of 20,000 Saints’. Along the way, they see spectacular landscapes, visit holy sites and engage in fasting, ritual and meditation.

programme.title: Wilderness with Simon Reeve
programme.desc: Simon Reeve journeys deep into Canada’s vast and empty Yukon territory – one of North America’s most iconic and remote landscapes. Covering an area almost the size of Spain but home to fewer than 50,000 people, the Yukon is a land of immense forests, glaciers, rivers and wildlife. In wealthy, modern Canada, Simon wants to find out how the people and the wildlife of this immense wilderness are faring - all while searching for an apex predator, the grizzly bear.

programme.title: Later... with Jools Holland
programme.desc: Jools is joined by Paul Heaton, Skye Newman, DC3, mary in the junkyard and Dermot Henry, and chats to Johnny Marr.

programme.title: Don't Look Now
programme.desc: Grieving the loss of their young daughter in a tragic accident, Laura and John Baxter visit Venice, where John is helping to restore a dilapidated church. As John works, Laura is befriended by two sisters, one of whom warns them to leave the city, claiming she has seen their dead daughter. Classic mystery thriller from Nicolas Roeg.

programme.title: Not Going Out
programme.desc: After receiving a Cameo birthday message from one of his comedy heroes, Nigel Planer, Lee does not realise that Lucy has paid for it. So, when he sees Nigel in a packed restaurant, he rushes over to introduce himself, assuming that they must now be best friends. This is news to Nigel.

programme.title: Question Time
programme.desc: Fiona Bruce presents an hour of debate from Peterlee in County Durham, with politicians, commentators and members of the public. On the panel are, from the government, the justice minister Jake Richards; the Conservative shadow Scottish secretary Harriet Cross; Max Wilkinson from the Liberal Democrats; the Daily Mirror’s associate editor Kevin Maguire; and the Telegraph’s senior political commentator Annabel Denham.

programme.title: Saving Lives at Sea
programme.desc: In Watergate Bay, one of Cornwall’s surfing hotspots, two teenage boys are caught in one of the beach’s notorious rip currents. When three distress signals are activated off the Pembrokeshire coast, the Fishguard crew race out to their location; en route, they discover there are seven kayakers in need of rescue, with winds gusting at 50 miles an hour. On one of the hottest days of the year, the Lyme Regis crew receive reports of a man suffering from heat stroke on a remote stretch of beach. And on the Isle of Wight, a fossil hunter is trapped waist deep in mud - with the tide steadily rising.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Indulge in a splash of seaside nostalgia with host Caroline Hawley and two more teams of antiques hunters. In Bristol, Caroline visits the Martin Parr Foundation to view a genre-defining exhibition by the late photographer Martin Parr CBE. It’s 40 years since Parr produced his iconic collection of images of working-class family holidays in the Merseyside resort of New Brighton. Parr’s radical style broke away from the professional black-and-white photography of the time, earning him both praise and criticism for his colour-rich images. Aiming to snap up bargains of their own in Warwickshire are two teams of family and friends. In red are pals and amateur actors David and Shawn with antiques expert David Fergus, and in blue are father and daughter-in-law Ollie and Perdie with their expert Thomas Forrester. With an hour to shop, the reds wonder if they’ll squeeze out a profit with a wooden juicer, while the blues decide whether a 1970s first-aid kit will remedy their challenge. In the saleroom, there are ups and downs for both teams until the bidders take a shine to one particular polished purchase.

programme.title: The Great House Revival
programme.desc: Architect duo Rob and Alfonso take on the task of restoring their historic terraced house into a stylish, contemporary home. Can they achieve their dream of creating a unique home and workspace with the perfect balance of old and new? Presented by Hugh Wallace.

programme.title: Match of the Day
programme.desc: Mark Chapman presents highlights of three Premier League games as well as September’s Goal of the Month. Manchester City face Liverpool in a highly charged fixture at Anfield, newly promoted Hull City are looking to continue their impressive start to the season at home to unbeaten Everton, and Nottingham Forest travel to Crystal Palace, who are so far without a win in the Premier League.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Politics Live
programme.desc: The big political issues of the day.

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: Game show presented by Rick Edwards in which players score points by answering questions correctly. However, they must avoid the Impossible answers, otherwise they will be eliminated from the show until the next day. In each episode, there are three rounds, and the three highest scorers from each round play against each other in the final. The winner of this battle faces a £10,000 question.

programme.title: The Answer Run
programme.desc: Comedian Jason Manford hosts an exciting, fast-paced quiz show, where three couples face a series of 50/50 questions which hurtle The Answer Run down towards them. Across three rounds, the couples build up their cash pots, but only one pair can face The Final Run and win the chance to take home their cash prize. Who will swipe their way to victory?

programme.title: The Boss
programme.desc: Susan Calman hosts the quiz show of tactics, knowledge and nerve. Contestants must work as a team, but ultimately there can only be one Boss. Who will pick off their opponents and walk away with the thousands of pounds on offer?

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo begins a railway tour of the spectacular border counties of Cumbria and Dumfriesshire, starting in the stunning Lake District National Park, where he discovers the violent geological history of volcanoes and colliding continents that shaped this breathtaking landscape. For an aerial view, he takes to the skies in a gyroplane - part plane, part helicopter. In Ambleside, at the National School of Forestry, Michael meets the trainees aspiring to become qualified foresters, and a visit to the heritage Lakeside and Haverthwaite Railway charts the region’s transformation from mining to tourism. Finally, Michael explores Sellafield, a key site in the UK’s nuclear history, and drives a train normally used to transport spent nuclear fuel across one of the largest private railway sidings in Europe.

programme.title: The Great House Revival
programme.desc: Paul buys back his former family home and takes on the mammoth task of restoring it himself. With dry rot, a leaking roof and rotten beams standing in his way, can he save his old childhood home, and his mother’s pride and joy, from ruin? Presented by Hugh Wallace.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel takes the Roadshow to visit Mount Stewart in Northern Ireland. Treasures include a valuable painting once thrown on a skip, a memento from Laurel and Hardy, and Henry Sandon is introduced to a mug bearing his spitting image.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Flog It! comes from Ragley Hall in Warwickshire, a beautiful 17th-century Palladian house owned by the Marquess of Hertford. Antiques experts Charlie Ross and Will Axon find great treasures among hundreds of visitors to the stately home. Charlie models an interesting Busby hat and Will gets a surprise when a Worcester coffee set goes under the hammer. Paul Martin explores the Battle of Edgehill.

programme.title: House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Chizzy Akudolu, Stephen Bailey, Banjo Beale and Philippa Dunne take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, Michael Sheen. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted with the brand new House of Games record player?

programme.title: Strictly - It Takes Two
programme.desc: Ellie Taylor has another week of behind-the-scenes exclusives and backstage Strictly gossip. She’s joined by the latest couple to be eliminated, and the panel of all-stars returns to break down all the weekend’s action.

programme.title: Global Eye
programme.desc: A weekly programme from the BBC World Service, bringing forensic journalism from all corners of the world by BBC Eye, the World Service's critically acclaimed investigative unit, and featuring expert global correspondents getting to the heart of the biggest international stories. In this episode: Nadine Yousif reports from Canada, where growing tensions over Alberta's place within the federation are fuelling a debate about identity, sovereignty and political power. As some push for greater autonomy and others warn against deepening divisions, Global Eye examines competing visions of Canada's future. Plus: we travel to the remote mountains of Papua, where the world's last tropical glaciers are rapidly disappearing, exploring what their loss means for Indigenous communities and a landscape undergoing profound change.

programme.title: Mastermind
programme.desc: Clive Myrie tests four more contenders on their specialist subjects and general knowledge in another Mastermind heat. The specialist subjects are The Lord of the Rings by JRR Tolkien, the band Talking Heads, the television series Foyle's War and the PDC World Darts Championship.

programme.title: Only Connect
programme.desc: Victoria Coren Mitchell hosts the quiz where knowledge only gets you so far – the vital extra ingredients are logic and lateral thinking. Nobody goes home after this episode – that’s just how the series structure rolls. The questions are as quirky as ever, for example: what connects panorama, accountant, unalive and seggs?

programme.title: University Challenge
programme.desc: The first round of the competition concludes with a match between SOAS University of London and Edinburgh. Amol Rajan asks the questions.

programme.title: Being Muslim After 9/11
programme.desc: After long careers exploring British Muslim life as journalists and film-makers, Mobeen Azhar and Masood Khan revisit their archive, reconnect with old interviewees and meet a wider range of people with important stories to tell, seeking to understand how things have changed for their community in the 25 years since 9/11.

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Paul and Bob fish the beautiful river Wensum in search of the equally beautifully roach. Struggling up and down the riverbanks, they realise how age is starting to take its toll on their physicality. But Bob has a plan to help Paul recapture his youth. They stay overnight in a disused train station and visit the local pub with Paul showing off his new look, courtesy of Bob. They decide to challenge each other to a fishing competition where the winner gets a very special culinary treat, and be warned, their dinner table conversation is not for the faint hearted.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the news stories of the day. With Victoria Derbyshire.

programme.title: American Fiction
programme.desc: Novelist Thelonious 'Monk' Ellison's books are well-reviewed and well-regarded, but they don't sell well, and he is in a rut. Despairing at the way other black authors are marketed and the way they're expected to write and behave, he pens a tough crime novel under a pseudonym, as a protest, expecting it to disappear. But things get out of hand when publishers love it, and his alter ego, the wanted felon Stagg R Leigh, is offered a huge advance.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Matt Baker and Emily McGowan are in the Cotswolds for the biggest date in the sheepdog trialling calendar - the Supreme. The finest dogs and handlers from across the UK and Ireland go head-to-head in a thrilling showcase of instinct, skill and control. After months of training and a year of tough qualifying trials, it all comes down to this - but only one will claim the coveted title of Supreme Champion.

programme.title: This is CBBC!
programme.desc: Tune every day from 7.00am.

programme.title: Shaun the Sheep
programme.desc: Another adventure with the mischievous young sheep and his flock. The Farmer decides to get a robotic sheepdog, but it turns out to be even stricter than Bitzer.

programme.title: Danger Mouse
programme.desc: When Danger Mouse makes short work of Burt Badboy and his newly acquired band of fanatical feline followers, the group's leader Mandy and her cult of cats immediately trade in their colourful mohican hairstyles for eyepatches and become Danger Mouse worshippers. At first Danger Mouse is having too much fun to take notice of Penfold's warnings about his new-found cult status, but even he is forced to act when the cats follow his example a little too literally and live life a little too dangerously. Danger Mouse's attempt to disown the cats goes down like a lead balloon, and they use mouse-fu skills and a superpowered amulet stolen from Tutenkamoo to show their idol the error of his ways. Danger Mouse battles the frenzied feline onslaught and saves HQ from becoming a giant scratching post. However, this only reaffirms the idea that he is the chosen one in the minds of Mandy and the cult of cats. Danger Mouse realises that the only solution is to find a new obsession for the cats.

programme.title: Dennis & Gnasher Unleashed!
programme.desc: Walter and Dennis go head to head in a sponsored silence. Being quiet doesn’t come naturally to either of them, as they struggle to make it through a chaotic school day and keep schtumm.

programme.title: Boy Girl Dog Cat Mouse Cheese
programme.desc: When Dog's old karate teacher retires, Dog decides that the perfect retirement gift would be to keep the sensei’s flame alive and pass on his karate talents - but that doesn’t go down too well with the rest of his reluctant family.

programme.desc: When pigeons won't leave the mayor’s statue alone, Duck and Frog are called in to get rid of them. However, when their attempts don't work, they have to get more creative.

programme.title: Duck and Frog
programme.desc: Working from home isn't easy for Duck when his video calls are constantly interrupted by Frog gaming loudly or trying to sneak past his desk to get to the snacks!

programme.desc: Joe and Shereen welcome the Stage Stars students into the studio for a morning of Mash-Up fun, there's a musical Joe v Shereen challenge, and don't miss a new Strictly Pro Dance Off!

programme.title: Blue Peter
programme.desc: Abby competes in the British Rowing Club Championships - can she pull off a gold medal performance? And Brainiac Live perform some mind-blowing science experiments.

programme.title: The Next Step: Cheer
programme.desc: When a legendary coach abruptly leaves a highly successful cheerleading gym, the team are left in disarray, The Next Step’s Kenzie steps in to take over what’s left of the team, desperate to prove she is more than just a dancer, and that she can build this rag-tag group of athletes into a contender for nationals.

programme.desc: When a legendary coach abruptly leaves a highly successful cheerleading gym, the team are left in disarray, The Next Step’s Kenzie steps in to take over what’s left of the team, desperate to prove she is more than just a dancer, and that she can build this rag-tag group of athletes into a contender for nationals.

programme.title: Malory Towers
programme.desc: Felicity and June follow a mysterious girl in uniform to Miss Grayling’s study, but she runs off. Miss Grayling checks her room, which appears to be in order - but what did the intruder want?

programme.title: Pickle Storm
programme.desc: Pickle faces a new challenge - her first day at school. Despite Mia’s help, Pickle struggles to fit in, and soon her magic is causing chaos and a monster is loose in the classroom!

programme.title: Game on Grandparents
programme.desc: Skilled kid gamers coach their novice grandparents to compete in an epic esports battle in the hope of becoming the GOAT of Game on Grandparents! Girls and boys who dream of playing at an eSports tournament are about to get the chance, but there is a twist - they won't be playing themselves but instead have to train their gran or grandad! While their grandparents are busy practising, the children have to take on their roles about the house, from washing up or walking the dog, to entertaining grandma’s friends for the afternoon – what could possibly go wrong?!

programme.title: Ocean's Eleven
programme.desc: Dapper Danny Ocean is a man of action. Less than 24 hours into his parole from a New Jersey penitentiary, the wry, charismatic thief is already rolling out his next plan. Danny orchestrates the most sophisticated, elaborate casino heist in history.

programme.title: Ocean's Twelve
programme.desc: After successfully robbing five casinos in one night, Danny Ocean and his crew of thieves have big problems. Despite pulling off one of the biggest heists in Las Vegas history, the members of the gang have already spent much of the money they stole. Casino owner Terry Benedict demands that Ocean return the money, plus millions more in interest. Unable to come up the cash, the crew is forced to come together to pull off another series of heists, this time in Europe.

programme.title: Ocean's Thirteen
programme.desc: Danny Ocean and his gang hatch an ambitious plot for revenge after ruthless casino owner Willy Bank double-crosses Reuben Tishkoff, Danny's friend and mentor. First, Ocean's gang plan to hit Bank in the paycheck by reversing the precept that the house always wins. Next, they will deal a crushing blow to Bank's ego by ruining his reputation as the only hotelier to earn the Royal Review's Five Diamond Award for each of his properties.

programme.title: Contagion
programme.desc: When Beth Emhoff returns to Minnesota from a Hong Kong business trip, she attributes the malaise she feels to jet lag. However, two days later, Beth is dead, and doctors tell her shocked husband that they have no idea what killed her. Soon, many others start to exhibit the same symptoms, and a global pandemic explodes. Doctors try to contain the lethal microbe, but society begins to collapse as a blogger fans the flames of paranoia.

programme.title: Prancer: A Christmas Tale
programme.desc: Ten-year-old Gloria and her recently widowed grandfather Bud befriend a mysterious reindeer when the family gathers for Christmas. Bud comes to believe that Prancer may actually be magical, but Gloria fears his theory will send him straight to a retirement home. They try to keep the secret while figuring out why the reindeer has appeared, and longstanding rifts within the family are healed along the way.

programme.title: The Man Who Invented Christmas
programme.desc: In 1843 London, author Charles Dickens finds himself in financial trouble after writing three unsuccessful novels in a row. Desperate for a hit, Dickens relies on real-life inspiration and his vivid imagination to bring Ebenezer Scrooge, Tiny Tim and other classic characters to life in "A Christmas Carol," forever changing the holiday season into the celebration known today.

programme.title: Chasing Mavericks
programme.desc: When 15-year-old surfing phenomenon Jay Moriarty discovers that the mythic Mavericks surf break, one of the biggest waves on Earth, actually exists near his California home, he becomes determined to conquer it. Jay enlists the aid of local surfing legend Frosty Hesson to train him to ride the Mavericks and live to tell about it. As Jay and Frosty carry on their quest to achieve the impossible, they develop a unique friendship that transforms both their lives.

programme.title: Atomic Blonde
programme.desc: Sensual and savage, Lorraine Broughton is the most elite spy in MI6, an agent who's willing to use all of her lethal skills to stay alive during an impossible mission. With the Berlin Wall about to fall, she travels into the heart of the city to retrieve a priceless dossier and take down a ruthless espionage ring. Once there, she teams up with an embedded station chief to navigate her way through the deadliest game of spies.

programme.title: Beetlejuice Beetlejuice
programme.desc: Still haunted by Beetlejuice, Lydia's life gets turned upside down when her daughter discovers a portal to the afterlife. When someone says Beetlejuice's name three times, the mischievous demon returns to unleash his very own brand of mayhem.

programme.title: Robin Hood
programme.desc: After the death of Richard the Lion-Hearted, a skilled archer named Robin Longstride travels to Nottingham, where villagers suffer under a despotic sheriff and crippling taxation. He meets and falls in love with a spirited widow, Marion, although she is skeptical of his motives. Hoping to win her heart and save the village, Robin gathers a band of warriors to fight corruption in Nottingham, little knowing they will soon be fighting to save England itself.

programme.title: Smoking Tigers
programme.desc: Lonely 16-year-old Korean American Hayoung tries to hide her problematic family and lower-income background from her new wealthy friends.

programme.title: A History of Violence
programme.desc: When a pair of petty criminals attempt to rob his small-town diner, Tom Stall (Viggo Mortensen) quickly and easily kills them both. In the flush of news coverage of Tom's seemingly heroic actions, a threatening stranger named Carl Fogarty (Ed Harris) comes to town, fingering the unassuming family man as long-missing Philadelphia mobster Joey Cusack. To the horror of his wife, Edie (Maria Bello), and teenage son, Jack (Ashton Holmes), Tom finds he must confront his violent past.

programme.title: Cleaner
programme.desc: Hoping to expose corruption, radical activists take 300 hostages at an energy company's annual gala in a high-rise building. Their cause soon gets hijacked by an extremist within their ranks who's ready to kill everyone. It's now up to a former soldier who works as a window cleaner to save the hostages trapped inside, including her younger brother.

programme.title: Room
programme.desc: Held captive for years in an enclosed space, a woman and her young son finally gain their freedom, allowing the boy to experience the outside world for the first time.

programme.title: Trap
programme.desc: A man and his teenage daughter realize they're at the center of a dark and sinister event while watching a concert.

programme.title: Enter Nowhere
programme.desc: Three strangers arrive one at a time in a remote cabin, and learn they have been brought together for a reason.

programme.title: Stonewall
programme.desc: Kicked out by his parents, a gay teenager (Jeremy Irvine) leaves small-town Indiana for New York's Greenwich Village, where growing discrimination against the LGBT community leads to riots on June 28, 1969.

programme.title: Fantastic Beasts: A Natural History
programme.desc: Delving into the mythological, including dragons, mermaids, and unicorns -- alongside examinations of natural world beasts, such as vervet monkeys, narwhals, and manatees; Stephen Fry travels far and wide to learn about such animals.

programme.title: Nanny McPhee Returns
programme.desc: Enigmatic Nanny McPhee arrives on the doorstep of a harried mother, Isabel Green, who is trying to raise her kids and tend to the family farm while her husband is away at war. Isabel has her hands full of not only her own three, but also with her sister's spoiled pair. With no time to lose, McPhee uses magic to instill in the children five important lessons.

programme.title: Epic
programme.desc: Mary Katherine (Amanda Seyfried), or M.K., is a headstrong, spirited teenager who has a strained relationship with her father (Jason Sudeikis). She loses patience with her dad's tales of unseen people who live in the woods, but when she is magically transported to that mythic realm, she gains new perspective. M.K. joins a race of beings known as the Leafmen in their battle to protect their queen (Beyoncé Knowles) from their enemies, evil Mandrake (Christoph Waltz) and his crew of Boggans.

programme.title: Mojave
programme.desc: A down-and-out artist (Garrett Hedlund) has a dangerous and shocking encounter with an evil drifter (Oscar Isaac) in the desert, leading to terrifying consequences when the deadly stranger follows his unsuspecting victim home.

programme.title: Arctic
programme.desc: A man stranded in the Arctic after an airplane crash must decide whether to remain in the relative safety of his makeshift camp or to embark on a deadly trek through the unknown in hopes of making it out alive.

programme.title: Life of Pi
programme.desc: After deciding to sell their zoo in India and move to Canada, Santosh and Gita Patel board a freighter with their sons and a few remaining animals. Tragedy strikes when a terrible storm sinks the ship, leaving the Patels' teenage son, Pi, as the only human survivor. However, Pi is not alone; a fearsome Bengal tiger has also found refuge aboard the lifeboat. As days turn into weeks and weeks drag into months, Pi and the tiger must learn to trust each other if both are to survive.

programme.title: Pan
programme.desc: Living a bleak existence at a London orphanage, 12-year-old Peter finds himself whisked away to the fantastical world of Neverland. Adventure awaits as he meets new friend James Hook and the warrior Tiger Lily. They must band together to save Neverland from the ruthless pirate Blackbeard.

programme.title: X-Men: First Class
programme.desc: In the early 1960s, during the height of the Cold War, a mutant named Charles Xavier (James McAvoy) meets a fellow mutant named Erik Lehnsherr (Michael Fassbender). Despite their vastly different backgrounds -- Charles grew up with a wealthy family, while Erik lost his parents at Auschwitz -- the two become close friends. As the world teeters on the brink of a nuclear war, Charles and Erik with other mutants join forces to save humanity. However, a situation soon tears the friends apart.

programme.title: Three Billboards Outside Ebbing, Missouri
programme.desc: After months have passed without a culprit in her daughter's murder case, Mildred Hayes makes a bold move, painting three signs leading into her town with a controversial message directed at William Willoughby, the town's revered chief of police. When his second-in-command, Officer Dixon -- an immature mother's boy with a penchant for violence -- gets involved, the battle is only exacerbated.

programme.title: Beirut
programme.desc: In the 1980s Beirut, Mason Skiles is a former U.S. diplomat who is called back into service to save a colleague from the group that is possibly responsible for his own family's death. Meanwhile, a CIA field agent who is working undercover at the American embassy is tasked with keeping Mason alive and ensuring that the mission is a success.

programme.title: The Perfect Match
programme.desc: Charlie (Terrence J) is a charming playboy who doesn't believe in serious relationships. His best friends bet him that if he commits to one woman for one month, he's bound to fall in love. Charlie accepts the seemingly easy challenge, but wasn't expecting to cross paths with the beautiful and mysterious Eva (Cassie Ventura). When Charlie coaxes her into a casual affair, Eva turns the tables on him, forcing the lifelong bachelor to question whether he wants more than just a one-night stand.

programme.title: Spring Breakers
programme.desc: College students Candy (Vanessa Hudgens), Faith (Selena Gomez), Brit (Ashley Benson) and Cotty (Rachel Korine) are short of the cash they need for a spring-break trip, so they rob a diner and head down to Florida. However, the police soon break up the party and arrest them. The curvaceous quartet are unexpectedly bailed out by a drug dealer and aspiring rap artist named Alien (James Franco). Soon after, three of the four gal pals decide to join Alien in a life of crime.

programme.title: Get Him to the Greek
programme.desc: An ambitious executive at a record company, Aaron Green (Jonah Hill) gets what looks like an easy assignment: He must escort British rock legend Aldous Snow (Russell Brand) to L.A.'s Greek Theatre for the first stop on a lucrative comeback-concert tour. Snow, however, has different plans. Learning his true love is in California, the rocker vows to win her back before starting the tour, forcing Aaron to pull out all the stops to get Snow on stage in time.

programme.title: Rampage
programme.desc: Primatologist Davis Okoye shares an unshakable bond with George, an extraordinarily intelligent, silverback gorilla that's been in his care since birth. When a rogue genetic experiment goes wrong, it causes George, a wolf and a reptile to grow to a monstrous size. As the mutated beasts embark on a path of destruction, Okoye teams up with a discredited genetic engineer and the military to secure an antidote and prevent a global catastrophe.

programme.title: Wonka
programme.desc: Armed with nothing but a hatful of dreams, young chocolatier Willy Wonka manages to change the world, one delectable bite at a time.

programme.title: DC League of Super-Pets
programme.desc: Krypto the Super-Dog and Superman are inseparable best friends, sharing the same superpowers and fighting crime side by side in Metropolis. However, when the Man of Steel and the rest of the Justice League are kidnapped, Krypto must convince a ragtag group of animals to master their own newfound powers for a rescue mission.

programme.title: Shazam!
programme.desc: We all have a superhero inside of us -- it just takes a bit of magic to bring it out. In 14-year-old Billy Batson's case, all he needs to do is shout out one word to transform into the adult superhero Shazam. Still a kid at heart, Shazam revels in the new version of himself by doing what any other teen would do -- have fun while testing out his newfound powers. But he'll need to master them quickly before the evil Dr. Thaddeus Sivana can get his hands on Shazam's magical abilities.

programme.title: Shazam! Fury of the Gods

When a vengeful trio of ancient gods arrives on Earth in search of the magic stolen from them long ago, Shazam and his allies get thrust into a battle for their superpowers, their lives, and the fate of the world.

programme.title: Black Adam

Nearly 5,000 years have passed, and Black Adam has gone from man to myth to legend. Now free, his unique form of justice, born out of rage, is challenged by modern-day heroes who form the Justice Society: Hawkman, Dr. Fate, Atom Smasher and Cyclone.

programme.title: The Flash
